title: Barclays cutting 5k jobs as it increases reliance on AI
content:
Barclays cutting 5,000 jobs as it increases reliance on AI
Barclays is cutting its staff by around 5,000 as it introduces more artificial intelligence (AI) into its work processes.
The banking group said 1,000 posts had already been closed and it expects a further reduction of 4,000 to be complete by the end of this year, amounting to around 5% of its global workforce.
The bank's cost reductions are focused on its UK retail bank, but some back office functions for the UK are done in India, where a significant proportion of the job cuts are expected to fall.
Barclays said the changes were the result of an ongoing modernisation plan, with the use of AI being the "icing on the cake" of its strategy.
The banking group is reaching the end of a three year cost-cutting programme focused primarily on its UK retail banking arm, although the investment banking division is also affected.
Barclays also revealed it made £2.3bn profit in the three months to September, higher than the same period a year ago, but slightly less than forecast.
Economists have been watching companies' results carefully for signs that investment in new technology, and AI specifically, is making a difference in their day-to-day operations, leading to greater efficiency and lower employment.
Barclays Group chief executive CS Venkatakrishnan said the job cuts were the result of significant investment it is making in technology to simplify and improve its business.
"AI has an important role to play and may have a more important role to play in the future.
"We will employ the AI at scale," he said. "But AI is the icing on the cake not the cake.
"Because you need to do the infrastructure build to get the benefits of AI."
Barclays said around 60% of the job cuts will fall within its support functions, including among developers.
Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell, said Barclays was "reaching for the AI lever, expecting to cut a decent chunk of its workforce as it expands the use of artificial intelligence", but had failed to match expectations with its financial results.
Will Howlett, financials analyst at Quilter Cheviot said the cuts illustrated "how significantly AI and automation could reshape the banking industry over the next few years".
"Banks have spent heavily on technology for years, but we are increasingly reaching the point where that investment translates into fewer people being required to run the business," he said.
Barclays said it expects its efficiency measures to deliver a further £1.1bn of savings in 2027.

report.summary: Barclays is cutting about 5,000 jobs, roughly 5% of its global workforce, as it scales AI and automation within a broader three-year cost-cutting plan.
report.background: Barclays is nearing the end of a three-year efficiency programme focused mainly on its UK retail bank, though investment banking is also affected. Banks have spent heavily on technology for years, but AI and automation are now reaching production scale, prompting scrutiny of whether tech investment finally lowers headcount. Barclays has already closed 1,000 roles and plans 4,000 more by year-end, around 5% of its global workforce. Cuts fall heavily on support functions, including developers, and some UK back-office work is done in India, so India is expected to absorb a significant share. The bank reported £2.3bn quarterly profit to September, higher year on year but slightly below forecasts. CEO CS Venkatakrishnan frames AI as the 'icing on the cake' atop infrastructure build, not the sole cause. Analysts say banking may be at an inflection point where technology spending translates into fewer people.
key_points: Barclays will reduce headcount by around 5,000, or about 5% of its global workforce. About 1,000 roles have already gone, and the remaining 4,000 are expected to be completed by the end of this year. The cuts are part of a three-year modernisation and cost-reduction programme, not a standalone AI layoff announcement.

CEO CS Venkatakrishnan described AI as the 'icing on the cake' rather than the cake itself. He said Barclays must first build infrastructure to benefit from AI at scale. That framing matters: the job cuts reflect broader simplification, automation and process redesign, with AI as an accelerant rather than the only driver.

Around 60% of cuts will hit support functions, including developers. The UK retail bank is the main focus, but some UK back-office work is performed in India, where a significant proportion of reductions is expected. This shows AI-enabled efficiency can hit both customer-facing operations and technical teams.

The bank reported £2.3bn profit for the three months to September, up year on year but slightly below forecasts. It expects efficiency measures to deliver another £1.1bn of savings in 2027. Analysts say results will be watched as evidence that heavy technology investment is finally translating into lower costs and headcount.

Analysts at AJ Bell and Quilter Cheviot see Barclays 'reaching for the AI lever' and automation reshaping banking over the next few years. The key question is whether banks can convert years of tech spending into measurable productivity gains without damaging service quality, controls or employee trust.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Barclays is a high-profile proof point that enterprise AI demand is tied to infrastructure, data plumbing, governance and workflow redesign—not just model access. It should boost vendors selling automation, cloud, model lifecycle and compliance tools. For developers, the signal is mixed: some support and developer roles are exposed, but demand shifts toward AI platform engineering, integration, evaluation and risk controls. For regular users, faster and cheaper banking may follow, but service quality, error handling and access to human support will be watched closely. The bigger lesson is that AI-driven efficiency is becoming a board-level workforce strategy, not an experiment.
report.tools: To follow the trend, watch enterprise AI orchestration and governance stacks rather than consumer chatbots: MLflow for model lifecycle, LangChain or LlamaIndex for LLM applications, Apache Airflow for workflow automation, and Open Policy Agent for policy controls. RPA platforms such as UiPath show how banks automate back-office tasks; open-source projects like Robot Framework, OpenBB and FinGPT offer hands-on ways to explore financial automation and AI.
